summary: Bulk internal access queue failing: Okta attribute canonicalization + LDAP identity-hash mismatch
description:
Issue summary:
A nightly bulk access-request batch (internal tool: Support Console bulk onboarding) started failing during the final provisioning step. The root trigger appears to be an Okta attribute canonicalization change in the last IdP rollout that altered case-folding for the 'employeeId' and 'mail' attributes; downstream LDAP connector compares an identity hash derived from those attributes and now rejects matches for ~17% of the batch.

Impact:
- ~120 internal user onboarding requests failed in last run; users stuck in 'Awaiting Provision' state.
- Affected workflows: runbook access for oncall, temporary feature-flag elevation, support dashboard login.
- Operational impact: Oncall escalation needed manual provisioning for high-priority users; estimated 90 minutes of engineering time so far.

Environment:
- Production (us-east) using Okta as IdP, internal SCIM bridge (scim-provisioner v2.7.1), LDAP-backed RBAC store (ldap-auth-connector v1.3.4).
- Related rollout: Okta attribute canonicalization change deployed 2026-03-13 (internal-idp-rollout-81).

Required fields present elsewhere in ticket. See steps_to_reproduce and logs for details.
steps_to_reproduce: Trigger bulk access queue via Support Console -> Bulk Onboarding -> Upload CSV with 200 entries (sample provided)
Monitor scim-provisioner logs during run: watch for 'identity-hash mismatch' warnings
Observe that 15-20% of users remain in 'Awaiting Provision' state with no retries succeeding
Inspect Okta user profile attributes; compare 'mail' and 'employeeId' casing to values received by SCIM bridge
observed_behavior: SCIM bridge computes identity-hash using Okta-provided attributes. When attribute case differs (uppercase letters in mailbox local-part or trailing whitespace trimmed differently), hash does not match LDAP entries and connector rejects provisioning with 400-level identity mismatch. Batch does not auto-retry because mismatch path is treated as non-transient.
expected_behavior: Attribute canonicalization should be normalized consistently between IdP and SCIM bridge, or SCIM bridge should implement tolerant matching (case-insensitive/email-normalization) for identity hash generation so bulk provisioning succeeds without manual intervention.
investigation_notes: 03/14 09:12: Observed spike in scim-provisioner warnings: 'identity-hash mismatch for user X (okta_id:00x)'.

03/14 09:20: Confirmed Okta rollout internal-idp-rollout-81 included attribute normalization that uppercases 'employeeId' for contractor mappings. Change communicated to Integrations but not to scim-provisioner team.

03/14 09:45: Reproduced locally with sample CSV: when Okta 'mail' payload has uppercase letters in local-part, scim-provisioner generates different identity-hash than LDAP (which stored lowercase-normalized emails).

Hypothesis A: Okta canonicalization changed input casing for select attributes causing deterministic hash divergence.
Hypothesis B: scim-provisioner uses raw attribute bytes for hashing rather than normalized form; introducing normalization would resolve mismatch without IdP rollback.
Temporary mitigation attempted: added a one-off transformation in provisioner stage to lowercase 'mail' before hashing; the subsequent small test run succeeded for previously failing rows (5/5).
comments: Evan Schultz (2026-03-14 09:30): Filing ticket after manual triage — ~120 rows failed during nightly run; attached CSV has sample rows. Prioritized because oncall users were affected.

Priya Nair (2026-03-14 09:40): Assigned. I reproduced an example locally by simulating Okta payloads — looks like casing differences cause the hash diverge. Starting with a narrow workaround (lowercase email in hashing pipeline) while we decide long-term fix.

Marco Alvarez (Identity Eng) (2026-03-14 10:05): Confirmed change in internal-idp-rollout-81. Okta mapping now preserves original case for 'mail' in some org profiles. Recommend adding normalization in scim-provisioner and a schema validation step to detect attribute-casing anomalies during preflight.

Priya Nair (2026-03-14 11:20): Rolled out canary of lowercase-normalization patch to scim-provisioner instances handling bulk queue (canary cluster). Test run with 20 rows showed 100% success for prior-failed cases. Monitoring for side effects — no regressions observed in first 40 minutes.
SRE (2026-03-14 12:05): Observed provisioner latency unchanged. Flagging for post-deploy security review — ensure normalization doesn't bypass email canonicalization rules used elsewhere.

Evan Schultz (2026-03-14 12:30): Noted a couple of contractor accounts still failing due to trailing whitespace in employeeId. Will strip whitespace in transformation and add fuzz test to CI for whitespace/case variants.
resolution: Mitigation in progress: scim-provisioner has a canary patch enabling attribute normalization (lowercase + trim) in hash generation. Long-term plan: update hashing to use canonical form (RFC5321 email normalization + employeeId trimming). Post-deploy follow-ups: add preflight detection for IdP attribute schema changes and coordinate a formal Okta mapping rollback plan if needed.
next_steps: Complete canary rollout for normalization patch across all scim-provisioner instances (Priya)
Add CI fuzz tests covering case/whitespace variations for identity-hash generation (Marco)
Publish runbook for detecting IdP canonicalization changes and notify integrators prior to rollouts (Ops)
Schedule postmortem and update provisioning runbook with normalization guidance (owner: Evan)
